# H9 todos

## Immediate theorem work

- State the Dense-Core Uniform-Decay Transfer Theorem with separate regulated, OS-reconstructed, and target-theory objects.
- Define the centered core (mathcal D_0), its physical Hilbert norm, and a state-separation criterion that rules out invisible spectral sectors.
- Prove that a norm-compatible bilinear decay bound on the dense core extends to (|e^{-tH}|_{Omega^perp}|\le e^{-mt}).
- Add the restricted-subspace conclusion for incomplete cores and formalize the (1.2) versus (0.4) overestimation mechanism.

## Uniformity obligations

- Express decay in physical time, including the cutoff-dependent conversion from transfer steps.
- Track constants uniformly in cutoff, volume, boundary condition, and retained history.
- Control normalization, short-time, and finite-volume errors strongly enough to pass to the continuum limit without loss of (m>0).
- Specify the core seminorm and prove that it is compatible with closure in the reconstructed physical Hilbert space.

## Continuum and identity obligations

- Establish the OS hypotheses for the limiting Euclidean correlations.
- Prove convergence of regulated temporal observables and transfer evolution to the OS-reconstructed vectors and semigroup.
- Identify the reconstructed observable algebra, vacuum sector, physical time, and Hamiltonian with those of the intended continuum Yang--Mills theory.
- Supply uniqueness or regulator-independence sufficient to exclude an auxiliary or subsequential gapped theory.

## Claim-control checks

- Label abstract transfer results and results conditional on continuum existence/identity as C2.
- Reserve C3 for the completed Yang--Mills construction with density, separation, uniform physical-time decay, and full-space extension all proved.
- Never infer the full physical gap from finitely many temporal probes or from decay on an unnamed invariant subspace.
